headline: Bond-tax report and a hawkish-leaning PBOC stall CGBs; policy banks cheapen 3bp, 10Y at 1.603%
summary: CGBs extended their pullback on Wednesday after a report that the PBOC is sounding out banks on taxing government bond interest, then steadied on Thursday as a RMB197bn overnight injection met a weaker stock market. Over the two sessions the CCDC 10-year rose 0.7bp to 1.603% (flat on the day) and the 30-year 1.8bp to 2.054%, with the 5-year (+1.9bp to 1.329%) and the long end leading while the 2-year held near 1.23%. Policy banks were the clear laggards: CDB 10-year rose 3.2bp on Thursday alone to about 1.688%, widening its spread over CGB to 8.5bp from 5.0bp on Tuesday, and ADBC and EXIM 10-year rose 2.5bp.
drivers: Bloomberg reported on Nov 11 that the PBOC surveyed lenders last month on how a 25% tax on CGB and local bond interest would hit their demand; it is unclear whether or when a levy comes. The 30-year future fell 0.43% that day and the CCDC 30-year rose 1.6bp; Huatai puts the full after-tax repricing of the 10-year at about 52bp but expects only 10–20bp on new issues.

CGBs were flat on Thursday while CDB, ADBC and EXIM rose 2.5–3.2bp across 5–20Y, so the CDB 10-year spread jumped 3.3bp to 8.5bp and the 7-year to 17bp. Wraps gave no single trigger; with funds and brokers still net sellers, it looks like crowded spread-tightening trades being unwound, since a CGB tax by itself should narrow, not widen, the gap to already-taxed policy bank bonds.

The Q3 monetary policy report kept the moderately loose stance and added RMB700bn of relending quota, but swapped language on new incremental policies for using existing tools together and flagged the risk of too-low rates; Citic sees this easing round as largely done. A column stressing that CGB yields must be read after tax added weight to the tax story.

After a RMB3bn drain on Wednesday, the PBOC injected a net RMB197bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% on Thursday ahead of the mid-month tax period; overnight Shibor held at 1.332% and 7-day rose 0.7bp to 1.397%. The Shanghai Composite fell 0.67% and ChiNext 2.44% after Wednesday's 3.1% ChiNext jump, which helped the 10-year steady.

view: Neutral for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.58–1.64% CCDC range. The tax headline and the PBOC's restraint on further easing cap the rally for now, but nothing is decided, funding stays anchored near the 1.25% overnight rate, inflation is soft and year-end allocation buying should absorb dips. I raise the 10-year buy level to 1.62–1.63% to allow for headline risk, keep the 5Y-into-10Y flattener and CGB over policy banks at 20–30Y, take profit on the CDB-into-CGB 10-year switch, and start leaning into cheaper policy bank 5–7Y spreads. An official tax plan would push the 10-year above 1.64% and narrow policy bank spreads, while weak October credit and activity data would take it back toward 1.58%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year is 1.226%, near its 1-year low (4th percentile, average 1.304%), and the 1-year slipped 0.3bp to 1.178%. The RMB197bn overnight injection kept funding just above the 1.25% anchor, but with the PBOC playing down further easing the front end has little room to rally.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s is −17.1bp (6th percentile, average −7.9bp) after the 5-year rose 1.9bp in two days to 1.329%, so the belly is cheapening from an extreme. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 27.4bp (53rd percentile, average 26.6bp), about 1.5bp in the money; 5s7s10s is −7.8bp (9th percentile), and a RMB150bn 7-year special CGB auction on Nov 18 adds belly supply.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year is 1.603%, 1.6bp above its 1-year low (2nd percentile), and peaked at 1.604% on Wednesday, so the old 1.61–1.62% buy level was not reached. Against neighbours it screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −25.4bp (79th percentile, average −29.4bp). I move the entry up 1bp for the tax headline risk.
buckets.call: Buy 10-year CGBs on a back-up to 1.62–1.63%, target 1.58%, stop 1.66%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year rose 1.8bp in two days to 2.054% and 10s30s is 45.1bp (38th percentile, average 45.8bp), while 30s50s fell to 11.1bp (5th percentile). The long end is most exposed to the tax story and leveraged fund selling, but insurer demand from mid-November supports it.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.03%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: Target hit: the CDB 10-year spread widened 3.3bp on Thursday to 8.5bp (54th percentile, average 9.7bp), through the 8bp target of the switch opened at ~3bp. At 2Y policy banks still sit near a 1-year tight (CDB 11.5bp, 1st percentile), so the curve of spreads is now fair at 10Y and rich only at the front.
buckets.call: Closed the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch at ~8.5bp; re-enter below 5bp, consider buying CDB above 12bp.

buckets.name: Policy banks 5–7Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 7-year rose 2.9bp to 1.597% and its spread over CGB jumped to 17.0bp (67th percentile, average 15.8bp); CDB 5-year is 14.1bp (50th percentile) and ADBC 5-year 16.0bp (68th). If a tax on CGB coupons were adopted, the gap to already-taxed policy bank bonds should narrow, which makes this widening a buying chance.
buckets.call: Buy CDB 7Y vs CGB 7Y at 17–18bp, target 14bp, stop 20.5bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.2bp more than CDB (63rd percentile, average 1.4bp) and EXIM 1.2bp (16th percentile, average 2.0bp), both 0.7bp tighter on Thursday as CDB led the sell-off. ADBC's Nov 11 10-year tap cleared at 1.6218% with 5.9 times cover, so demand is solid but the pickup has shrunk by about 1bp this week.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC 10Y over CDB 10Y; switch back to CDB if the pickup falls below 1bp. EXIM no longer offers value.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 7.3bp over CGB after widening 2.4bp on Thursday, still only the 14th percentile against a 10.5bp average; the 30-year spread is 11.0bp, below its 12.6bp average. The move is in favour of the trade but the cushion is still thin.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; take profit at a 10bp 20-year spread, stop below 5bp.
